title: Rotlewi vs Rubinstein, Łódź 1907
outcomes: Predicts Black's key moves in a real game from the position alone, before seeing them
Counts the pieces that guard the bishop on e4 and the pawn on h2 at each stage of the combination
Names the core idea (an overloaded queen, exploited by removing a defender and offering a rook) at the decisive moment

steps.text: **Rotlewi vs Rubinstein, Łódź, 1907.** Gersz Rotlewi had White, Akiba Rubinstein had Black, and Black won in 25 moves (White resigned). The next board plays the first twenty moves. Then you are asked for Black's move five times, without being told which idea to use, and after each answer a board shows what the game did. The moves come from two sources that agree on every one of them.

steps.caption: Moves 1 to 20. The last position is where your first decision comes (Black to move).

line.say: The game starts with the queen's pawn.
Black challenges White's centre pawn at once.
Black recaptures with the bishop.
The pawn on b4 attacks Black's bishop.
The bishop steps back to d6.
Black castles.
Black takes the pawn on c4.
White's bishop takes it back.
The b-pawn attacks the bishop.
The bishop returns to d3.
Black's rook takes the d-file.
Black's knight goes to e5.
Knights are traded and the bishop recaptures on e5.
White's f-pawn attacks the bishop on e5.
The bishop steps back to c7. Now the rook on d8 attacks the bishop on d3.
The pawn on e5 attacks the knight on f6.
The bishop gives check along the diagonal.
White's king steps into the corner. Now your first decision.

claims.statement: After 17...Bc7 the rook on d8 attacks the bishop on d3.
After 19.e5 the pawn attacks the knight on f6.

steps.caption: What the game did at move 20 and White's reply.

line.say: The knight leaves the pawn's attack and now attacks h2, which only the king defends.
White plays Be4. Had the queen taken on g4 instead, the bishop on d3 would have been loose.

claims.statement: After 20...Ng4 the knight attacks h2.
Only the king defends h2.
After Qxg4 the bishop on d3 is loose.

steps.caption: After 21...Qh4, White to move. If White passed, Black would play Qxh2, mate.

line.say: White attacks the queen. The pawn move also lets the queen on e2 guard h2 along the second rank.

claims.statement: If White passed, Qxh2 would be mate.
After g3 the pawn attacks the queen on h4.
After g3 the king and the queen defend h2.

line.say: Rxc3: the rook takes the knight. The bishop on e4 now has one defender, the queen.
White takes the queen. The queen on e2 is now the only guard of the bishop on e4.

claims.statement: After Rxc3 only the queen defends e4.
After gxh4 the queen is still the only defender of e4.

steps.caption: A line White did not play: 23.Bxc3 instead of 23.gxh4. The queen would be the only guard of e4 and one of two guards of h2.

line.say: If White takes the rook instead, the queen alone guards e4 and still helps guard h2.
Bxe4+ takes the bishop with check.
If the queen takes the bishop, it has left h2.

claims.statement: After Bxc3 only the queen defends e4.
After Bxc3 the king and the queen defend h2.
After Bxe4 the bishop gives check to the king on h1.
After Qxe4 only the king defends h2.
After Qxe4 the queen and the knight attack h2.

steps.caption: The position after 23.Bxc3 Bxe4+ 24.Qxe4. Black to move.

line.say: Qxh2 is checkmate: the knight on g4 guards the queen.

claims.statement: Qxh2 is checkmate.
After Qxh2 the knight on g4 guards the queen.

steps.caption: Black's moves 23 to 25 and White's replies.

line.say: Rd2 attacks the queen, which is the only guard of the bishop on e4.
The queen takes the rook and leaves e4. No White piece now defends that bishop.
Black takes the bishop, giving check along the long diagonal to h1.
White blocks the check with the queen.

claims.statement: After Rd2 the rook attacks the queen.
The queen still defends e4 after Rd2.
After Qxd2 nothing defends e4.

steps.caption: After 25...Rh3, White to move; White resigned here. The threat is Rxh2 mate. The bishop on e4 pins the queen on g2, so it cannot take on h2.

claims.statement: If White passed, Rxh2 would be mate.
The queen on g2 can move only along the diagonal of the pin.
At depth 16 the engine finds a forced mate for Black against every White move, in at most four moves.

steps.text: **What the game used.** **Counting attackers and defenders**: the bishop on e4 had two defenders, then one, then none. **Overloaded defender** (one piece guarding two things at once): after 22.g3 the queen on e2 defended both e4 and h2. **Removing a defender**: 22...Rxc3 took the knight. **Deflection**: 23...Rd2 attacked the queen, so taking the rook left e4 undefended. At depth 16 the engine rated Black over 2.5 pawns ahead before 20...Ng4 and over 10 ahead after 23.gxh4.

steps.prompt: Which moment would you have missed: 20...Ng4, 21...Qh4, 22...Rxc3, 23...Rd2 or 25...Rh3? Pick one, and write what you would have needed to notice.
